consequences_for_maestro: Enforcement granularity is a DIRECTORY. A flat branch name forces refs/heads/ to be writable, which grants the implementer every branch including the integration target. Maestro currently names implementer branches flat (orchestrator.py:1470 'impl-<task>-<ts>', selfheal 'selffix-<id>', 'redo-<id>'); they must become namespaced ('impl/<task>-<ts>') before enforced confinement is possible.

The shared object store must be writable by every confined implementer, so two concurrent implementers share one writable object directory. Git's object writes are content-addressed and additive, so this does not corrupt, but it is not isolation: one implementer can observe another's loose objects.
The parent directory of the branch namespace must exist before the sandbox starts, or there is nothing to bind.

A profile that masks a parent and binds a child gives the sandbox WRITABLE tmpfs intermediates: a forbidden write then silently succeeds and vanishes, which an agent reports as success. Mask leaves, or verify the mount plan; a silent no-op is worse than an error.
